## System Map: kvstore

### Repo path
`<<BLARE_WORKTREE_ROOT>>`

Source lives under `kvstore/`; build metadata in `BUILD.bazel` and `requirements.txt` at repo root. A `.blare/` directory also exists at the root, but it is the *analysis tool's own* working state (system-map.yaml, metrics.yaml, coverage.yaml, etc.) — not part of the kvstore service, so it is excluded from the map below.

### Service name and purpose
**kvstore** — a deliberately small, single-process, in-memory-cache-over-flat-file key-value store written in Python. Its only client-facing operation is `get_value(key)`. Per `kvstore/__init__.py` and `README.md`, it is explicitly a fixture codebase built to exercise an observability-analysis tool, containing several intentional, realistic bugs (each multiple hops upstream of an obvious symptom) rather than being a production service. There is no HTTP server, no process entrypoint script, and no container/orchestration config anywhere in the repo (no Dockerfile, docker-compose, k8s manifests, or terraform were found) — everything is a plain Python library invoked in-process by an unseen caller.

### Components

| ID | Kind | Description | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get-value-api` | entrypoint | The only client-facing function, `get_value(cache, key)`. Wraps `Cache.get`, catches `StorageError`, and increments a Prometheus counter labeled by outcome (`success`/`error`). | `kvstore/api.py:26-33` |
| `cache` | service | In-memory `Cache` class fronting `Storage`. `get()` checks its own dict first, falling back to storage only on a miss; never re-validates a cached entry. Exposes `items()` and `evict()` for the evictor. | `kvstore/cache.py:25-48` |
| `storage` | service | `Storage` class implementing `get`/`put` against a backing flat file, raising `StorageError` on OS-level read/write failures. | `kvstore/storage.py:16-46` |
| `kv-flat-file` | datastore | The actual backing datastore: a single delimited text file (one `key,value` pair per line) at a `Path` supplied to `Storage.__init__`. Read via `path.read_text()`, written via `path.write_text()` (full rewrite each `put`). No external DB — this is local disk state owned by the service. | `kvstore/storage.py:20-45` |
| `evictor` | job | `run_eviction_pass(cache)` — a background pass meant to be invoked periodically (e.g. by a scheduler loop) that walks `Cache.items()` and evicts entries older than `TTL_SECONDS` (300s). No scheduler/cron code is present in-repo; this is a callable meant to be driven externally. | `kvstore/evictor.py:12-32` |
| `admin-write-path` | entrypoint | `update_value(storage, cache, key, value)` — an internal, non-client-facing write path. Only calls `storage.put`; does **not** call `cache.evict`, despite receiving `cache` as a parameter. Explicitly documented as not reachable from external clients. | `kvstore/admin.py:12-16` |
| `data-sync-job` | job (external, inferred) | A periodic external job, not present in this repo, that is documented as the caller of `admin.update_value`. Its code is out of scope/not included here — inferred purely from docstrings. | `kvstore/__init__.py:6-7`, `kvstore/admin.py:1-3` |
| `prometheus-metrics-client` | external-dependency | `prometheus_client` library (pinned `==0.26.0`) used to define and increment `kvstore_get_value_requests_total{outcome}`, a `Counter`. No metrics-server/exporter code is present in-repo (no HTTP `/metrics` endpoint, no pushgateway client) — only the in-process counter object is defined; scraping/exposition is external and unimplemented here. | `requirements.txt:1`; `kvstore/api.py:14,19-23` |

### depends_on relationships

- `get-value-api -> cache` — `get_value` calls `cache.get(key)` directly. (`kvstore/api.py:28`)
- `get-value-api -> prometheus-metrics-client` — increments `GET_VALUE_REQUESTS` counter on both success and error paths. (`kvstore/api.py:19-32`)
- `cache -> storage` — on a cache miss, `Cache.get` calls `self._storage.get(key)` and populates the cache with the result. (`kvstore/cache.py:30-36`)
- `storage -> kv-flat-file` — `Storage.get`/`Storage.put` read/write the file at `self._path` via `Path.read_text`/`Path.write_text`, wrapping `OSError` as `StorageError`. (`kvstore/storage.py:20-45`)
- `evictor -> cache` — `run_eviction_pass` iterates `cache.items()` and calls `cache.evict(key)` for expired entries. (`kvstore/evictor.py:26-31`)
- `admin-write-path -> storage` — `update_value` calls `storage.put(key, value)`. (`kvstore/admin.py:16`)
- `admin-write-path -> cache` (declared but unused) — `update_value` accepts `cache` as a parameter but never calls `cache.evict`; this is a documented gap causing stale reads after writes until natural TTL expiry (which itself never fires — see below). (`kvstore/admin.py:8-16`, `kvstore/cache.py:44-47`)
- `data-sync-job -> admin-write-path` — inferred external caller relationship; the periodic data-sync job is documented as the consumer of `admin.update_value`, though its own code is not in this repo. (`kvstore/__init__.py:6-7`)
- (implicit, unimplemented) `evictor -> scheduler` — `run_eviction_pass` is designed to be invoked by "a scheduler loop," but no scheduler/cron entrypoint exists in the repo; nothing currently calls `evictor.py` at all as far as source code shows.

### Notable structural findings (relevant to observability mapping)
- No network entrypoints exist in this repo (no HTTP/gRPC server, no message consumer). `get_value` and `update_value` are plain function calls; whatever process embeds this library is out of scope/not present.
- Only one metric exists in the whole codebase (`kvstore_get_value_requests_total`), on the read path only. Per `kvstore/api.py:1-9` and `kvstore/cache.py:1-8`, none of the following failure modes emit any signal: stale reads after a write (cache/admin-write-path gap above), unbounded cache growth (evictor's TTL bug — `entry.inserted_at_ms` is stored in milliseconds but compared against `time.time()` in seconds at `kvstore/evictor.py:4-9,28`, so the expiry condition is never true and nothing is ever evicted), and key collisions in storage (last-write-wins dict rebuild in `Storage.put`, `kvstore/storage.py:33-39`).
- `admin-write-path` and `evictor` are both currently orphaned from any visible caller in-repo — their real invocation (a scheduler, a sync job) lives outside this codebase, which matters for any system map since those edges can only be asserted from documentation, not from traceable code.
- Build tooling (`BUILD.bazel`) exposes the repo's raw files as a Bazel `filegroup` (`kvstore_files`) consumed by an external test suite (`tests/e2e/kvstore_fixtures.py`, `tests/release/kvstore_repo.py`) belonging to the observability-analysis tool itself, not to kvstore — this is tooling plumbing, not a service dependency, and was excluded from the component list above.

payload_or_id.description: The only client-facing operation: get_value(cache, key). Calls Cache.get, catches StorageError (recording outcome=error) and re-raises it, and increments a Prometheus counter labeled by outcome (success/error) on every call.

In-memory dict-backed Cache fronting Storage. get() checks the in-memory dict first and returns immediately on hit, falling back to storage only on a miss and caching whatever storage returns (including None). Exposes items() and evict() but nothing in the write path calls evict().

Storage class implementing get/put against a backing flat file. Wraps OS-level read/write failures as StorageError. get() treats a missing file as an empty store (returns None) rather than an error. put() performs a full read-modify-write of the entire file with no locking or atomic rename.

Backing datastore: a single local text file storing one 'key,value' pair per line, unescaped. Read wholesale via Path.read_text() and rewritten wholesale via Path.write_text() on every put. Local disk state owned by the service; never shrinks (no delete/TTL at the storage layer).

run_eviction_pass(cache): a background pass intended to be invoked periodically by an external scheduler to TTL-expire cache entries older than TTL_SECONDS (300s). No scheduler/cron/invocation code exists anywhere in this repo.

update_value(storage, cache, key, value): internal, non-client-facing write path invoked by an external periodic sync job. Calls storage.put(key, value) only; never calls cache.evict(key) despite receiving cache as a parameter, so already-cached readers keep seeing the old value indefinitely. Has no error handling of its own.
Periodic external job, not present in this repository, documented as the caller of admin.update_value. Its scheduling, error handling, and cadence are unverifiable from this codebase.

Inferred external scheduler/cron mechanism intended to invoke evictor.run_eviction_pass() periodically. No such invocation exists anywhere in this repo; its existence and cadence cannot be confirmed from source.

payload_or_id.title: Backing file OS-level read/write fails
payload_or_id.description: The kv flat-file's OS-level read or write fails (disk full, permission denied, filesystem error, path removed under the running process). Storage.get/Storage.put catch OSError and re-raise as StorageError, proving this is an anticipated real condition (kvstore/storage.py:29-30,44-45).

payload_or_id.title: Configured storage path does not exist
payload_or_id.description: The configured storage file path is wrong, unmounted, or was deleted out-of-band. Storage.get treats a missing file as an empty store and returns None rather than raising (kvstore/storage.py:22-23), so misconfiguration is indistinguishable from an empty but healthy store.

payload_or_id.title: Evictor TTL comparison uses mismatched time units
payload_or_id.description: Entry.inserted_at_ms is stored in milliseconds (cache.py:35) but evictor.py computes 'now' in seconds and compares now - inserted_at_ms > TTL_SECONDS, always a large negative number, so the expiry condition is never true (kvstore/evictor.py:4-9,24-29).

payload_or_id.title: Evictor's periodic invocation is not present in-repo
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass(cache) takes no scheduling wiring and no cron/timer/scheduler-loop invoking it exists anywhere in this codebase. Whether, and how often, it runs at all is entirely external and unverifiable from source (kvstore/evictor.py:21-32).

payload_or_id.title: Admin write path never invalidates the cache
payload_or_id.description: admin.update_value() calls only storage.put(key, value); it never calls cache.evict(key) even though Cache exposes exactly that method for this purpose (kvstore/admin.py:12-16, kvstore/cache.py:42-48).

payload_or_id.title: Storage line format does not escape its delimiter
payload_or_id.description: Storage serializes each entry as 'key,value' joined by newlines and parses with a single partition(','), with no escaping of embedded ',' or '\n' in keys or values (kvstore/storage.py:24-27,36-43).

payload_or_id.title: Storage.put performs a non-atomic whole-file read-modify-write
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() reads the entire file, mutates a dict, and rewrites the entire file with write_text -- no file locking, no atomic temp-file+rename, no fsync, and two unsynchronized I/O operations (kvstore/storage.py:32-45).

payload_or_id.title: Storage has no TTL/delete and scans linearly
payload_or_id.description: The storage layer never removes entries; every key ever written persists forever. get() is an O(n) scan of every line and put() rewrites the whole file (also O(n)) on every write (kvstore/storage.py:20-45).

payload_or_id.title: No logging exists anywhere in the package
payload_or_id.description: There is no logging call anywhere in kvstore. The only instrumentation is a single Prometheus counter incremented solely on StorageError from the read path; every other failure mode leaves it untouched, actively masking rather than flagging them (kvstore/api.py:5-9,19-23).

payload_or_id.title: StorageError propagates out of the storage layer
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get/Storage.put convert an OSError into a StorageError and propagate it to their caller (Cache.get or admin.update_value) (kvstore/storage.py:29-30,44-45).

payload_or_id.title: No cache entry is ever removed by eviction
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass computes an empty expired_keys list every time it runs, if it runs at all, so no cache entry is ever removed once inserted (kvstore/evictor.py:25-29).

payload_or_id.title: get_value raises an unhandled exception to its caller
payload_or_id.description: api.get_value() catches StorageError only to record outcome=error and then re-raises it -- no fallback, no retry, no default value. The exception propagates unhandled out of the only public entrypoint (kvstore/api.py:26-33).

payload_or_id.title: Cache memory grows without bound under unique-key traffic
payload_or_id.description: Under sustained unique-key traffic, Cache._entries grows without bound since every miss inserts an entry and nothing ever removes one, risking OOM, process death, or GC-pressure-driven latency degradation (kvstore/cache.py:30-36).

payload_or_id.title: Reads keep returning a stale value after a write
payload_or_id.description: Cache.get() never re-consults storage once a key is cached. Combined with the admin write path not invalidating the cache, any value updated via admin.update_value is invisible to get_value forever for callers who already read that key, since eviction never fires either (kvstore/cache.py:30-33, kvstore/admin.py:13-15).

payload_or_id.title: A key first read as absent stays 'not found' forever after being written
payload_or_id.description: A key absent at first read gets cached as an entry with value=None, since storage.get returning None is cached like any other value. If that key is written later via admin.update_value, get_value keeps returning None forever -- worse than plain staleness because it looks like correct 'not found' behavior (kvstore/cache.py:34-36).

payload_or_id.title: get_value silently returns None for all data due to path misconfiguration
payload_or_id.description: If the storage file path is wrong, unmounted, or deleted, Storage.get() returns None for every key rather than raising, so get_value succeeds (outcome=success) while silently returning nothing for all data -- worse than a visible outage since the metric actively reports health (kvstore/storage.py:22-23).

payload_or_id.title: Embedded delimiter characters corrupt or collide storage entries
payload_or_id.description: A value containing an embedded newline splits across the one-line-per-entry format and is mis-parsed as extra lines on the next read, potentially shadowing or colliding with another key; a key containing a comma is truncated by partition(','), silently targeting the wrong row. No exception is raised in either case (kvstore/storage.py:24-27,36-43).

payload_or_id.title: Concurrent writes silently lose an update
payload_or_id.description: Two concurrent callers of storage.put/admin.update_value each read the same pre-write file state, then each rewrite the whole file -- the second writer's write_text completely overwrites the first writer's change with no error to either caller (kvstore/storage.py:33-43).

payload_or_id.title: A process crash mid-write truncates or corrupts the backing file
payload_or_id.description: write_text is not atomic (no temp-file+rename). If the process dies mid-write (kill, crash, OOM-kill -- a realistic trigger given unbounded cache growth -- or host failure), the file is left truncated. Storage has no checksum or validation and silently parses whatever partial content remains as valid data on the next call.

payload_or_id.title: A concurrent read observes a partially-written file
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put()'s read_text() and write_text() are two separate, unsynchronized operations. A concurrent Storage.get() from a different Cache miss can execute its own read_text() while a put() is mid-write_text(), observing a partially-written file. Narrower timing window than the lost-update case, hence lower severity (kvstore/storage.py:32-45).

payload_or_id.title: get_value latency degrades gradually as the store grows
payload_or_id.description: Because storage never removes entries and both get (linear scan) and put (full rewrite) are O(total keys), sustained unique-key write volume makes every get_value call progressively slower over the service's lifetime -- a gradual, silent latency/CPU trend with no counter tracking file size or call latency.

payload_or_id.title: Admin write failures are silent to whoever runs the sync job
payload_or_id.description: admin.update_value() has zero error handling -- a StorageError from storage.put() propagates straight out with no log line and no metric. Whether the external periodic sync-job caller handles or swallows it is unknowable from this codebase; either way nothing in kvstore records that the write was attempted or failed (kvstore/admin.py:12-16).

Storage.get/Storage.put catch OSError and re-raise as StorageError, proving this is an anticipated real condition (kvstore/storage.py:29-30,44-45). No metric distinguishes this root cause from other error causes, and the admin write path isn't instrumented at all.

payload_or_id.title: Configured storage path does not exist
payload_or_id.description: The configured storage file path is wrong, unmounted, or was deleted out-of-band. Storage.get treats a missing file as an empty store and returns None rather than raising (kvstore/storage.py:22-23), so misconfiguration is indistinguishable from an empty but healthy store. No signal exists today; needs a startup/periodic existence check or an emptiness-rate metric.

payload_or_id.title: Evictor TTL comparison uses mismatched time units
payload_or_id.description: Entry.inserted_at_ms is stored in milliseconds (cache.py:35) but evictor.py computes 'now' in seconds and compares now - inserted_at_ms > TTL_SECONDS, always a large negative number, so the expiry condition is never true (kvstore/evictor.py:4-9,24-29). Needs a cache-size or eviction-count metric to surface.

payload_or_id.title: Evictor's periodic invocation is not present in-repo
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass(cache) takes no scheduling wiring and no cron/timer/scheduler-loop invoking it exists anywhere in this codebase. Whether, and how often, it runs at all is entirely external and unverifiable from source (kvstore/evictor.py:21-32). Needs a last-run-timestamp/heartbeat metric for the eviction job.

payload_or_id.title: Admin write path never invalidates the cache
payload_or_id.description: admin.update_value() calls only storage.put(key, value); it never calls cache.evict(key) even though Cache exposes exactly that method for this purpose (kvstore/admin.py:12-16, kvstore/cache.py:42-48). Needs a cache-invalidation-count or staleness metric.

payload_or_id.title: Storage line format does not escape its delimiter
payload_or_id.description: Storage serializes each entry as 'key,value' joined by newlines and parses with a single partition(','), with no escaping of embedded ',' or '\n' in keys or values (kvstore/storage.py:24-27,36-43). Needs a parse/validation-error counter.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.put performs a non-atomic whole-file read-modify-write
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() reads the entire file, mutates a dict, and rewrites the entire file with write_text -- no file locking, no atomic temp-file+rename, no fsync, and two unsynchronized I/O operations (kvstore/storage.py:32-45). Needs a concurrent-writer/write-conflict metric.

payload_or_id.title: Storage has no TTL/delete and scans linearly
payload_or_id.description: The storage layer never removes entries; every key ever written persists forever. get() is an O(n) scan of every line and put() rewrites the whole file (also O(n)) on every write (kvstore/storage.py:20-45). Needs a store-size or per-call-latency metric.

payload_or_id.title: No logging exists anywhere in the package
payload_or_id.exclusion_reason: Cross-cutting instrumentation deficiency, not a discrete detectable event of its own -- remediated by the metric/logging additions recommended for the individual failure modes it currently masks (e.g. fm-admin-write-failure-silent-to-operators, fm-get-value-returns-none-for-existing-data), rather than by a standalone alert.
payload_or_id.description: There is no logging call anywhere in kvstore. The only instrumentation is a single Prometheus counter incremented solely on StorageError from the read path; every other failure mode leaves it untouched, actively masking rather than flagging them (kvstore/api.py:5-9,19-23).

payload_or_id.title: StorageError propagates out of the storage layer
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get/Storage.put convert an OSError into a StorageError and propagate it to their caller (Cache.get or admin.update_value) (kvstore/storage.py:29-30,44-45). Today only the get-value path's occurrences are counted (via outcome=error); the admin write path raises the same error with zero instrumentation, so full coverage needs a caller-agnostic counter.

payload_or_id.title: No cache entry is ever removed by eviction
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass computes an empty expired_keys list every time it runs, if it runs at all, so no cache entry is ever removed once inserted (kvstore/evictor.py:25-29). Needs a cache entry-count or oldest-entry-age metric.

payload_or_id.title: get_value raises an unhandled exception to its caller
payload_or_id.description: api.get_value() catches StorageError only to record outcome=error and then re-raises it -- no fallback, no retry, no default value. The exception propagates unhandled out of the only public entrypoint (kvstore/api.py:26-33). Already instrumented via kvstore_get_value_requests_total{outcome=error}; an alert can be defined on this counter today.

payload_or_id.title: Cache memory grows without bound under unique-key traffic
payload_or_id.description: Under sustained unique-key traffic, Cache._entries grows without bound since every miss inserts an entry and nothing ever removes one, risking OOM, process death, or GC-pressure-driven latency degradation (kvstore/cache.py:30-36). Needs a cache size or process memory metric.

payload_or_id.title: Reads keep returning a stale value after a write
payload_or_id.description: Cache.get() never re-consults storage once a key is cached. Combined with the admin write path not invalidating the cache, any value updated via admin.update_value is invisible to get_value forever for callers who already read that key, since eviction never fires either (kvstore/cache.py:30-33, kvstore/admin.py:13-15). Needs a staleness/invalidation metric.

payload_or_id.title: A key first read as absent stays 'not found' forever after being written
payload_or_id.description: A key absent at first read gets cached as an entry with value=None, since storage.get returning None is cached like any other value. If that key is written later via admin.update_value, get_value keeps returning None forever -- worse than plain staleness because it looks like correct 'not found' behavior (kvstore/cache.py:34-36). Needs a negative-cache-hit metric.

payload_or_id.title: get_value silently returns None for all data due to path misconfiguration
payload_or_id.description: If the storage file path is wrong, unmounted, or deleted, Storage.get() returns None for every key rather than raising, so get_value succeeds (outcome=success) while silently returning nothing for all data -- worse than a visible outage since the metric actively reports health (kvstore/storage.py:22-23). Needs a not-found-rate metric distinct from the current success/error counter.

payload_or_id.title: Embedded delimiter characters corrupt or collide storage entries
payload_or_id.description: A value containing an embedded newline splits across the one-line-per-entry format and is mis-parsed as extra lines on the next read, potentially shadowing or colliding with another key; a key containing a comma is truncated by partition(','), silently targeting the wrong row. No exception is raised in either case (kvstore/storage.py:24-27,36-43). Needs a parse-error/validation counter.

payload_or_id.title: Concurrent writes silently lose an update
payload_or_id.description: Two concurrent callers of storage.put/admin.update_value each read the same pre-write file state, then each rewrite the whole file -- the second writer's write_text completely overwrites the first writer's change with no error to either caller (kvstore/storage.py:33-43). Needs a concurrent-write/write-conflict metric.

payload_or_id.title: A process crash mid-write truncates or corrupts the backing file
payload_or_id.description: write_text is not atomic (no temp-file+rename). If the process dies mid-write (kill, crash, OOM-kill -- a realistic trigger given unbounded cache growth -- or host failure), the file is left truncated. Storage has no checksum or validation and silently parses whatever partial content remains as valid data on the next call. Needs a file-integrity/checksum-validation metric plus process restart/OOM tracking.

payload_or_id.title: A concurrent read observes a partially-written file
payload_or_id.exclusion_reason: Detecting a torn read specifically would require request-level tracing impractical for this metric surface. Its root cause (missing write locking) is already covered by the alert recommended for fm-concurrent-write-lost-update; a dedicated alert here would be redundant.
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put()'s read_text() and write_text() are two separate, unsynchronized operations. A concurrent Storage.get() from a different Cache miss can execute its own read_text() while a put() is mid-write_text(), observing a partially-written file (kvstore/storage.py:32-45).

payload_or_id.title: get_value latency degrades gradually as the store grows
payload_or_id.description: Because storage never removes entries and both get (linear scan) and put (full rewrite) are O(total keys), sustained unique-key write volume makes every get_value call progressively slower over the service's lifetime -- a gradual, silent latency/CPU trend with no counter tracking file size or call latency. Needs a latency histogram and/or store-size metric.

payload_or_id.title: Admin write failures are silent to whoever runs the sync job
payload_or_id.description: admin.update_value() has zero error handling -- a StorageError from storage.put() propagates straight out with no log line and no metric. Whether the external periodic sync-job caller handles or swallows it is unknowable from this codebase; either way nothing in kvstore records that the write was attempted or failed (kvstore/admin.py:12-16). Needs an admin-write error counter/log.

event.text:
All 22 FailureMode entries for Phase 2 are confirmed committed (verified via duplicate-id probes on the first, last, and second-to-last entries in the batch).

## Phase 2 summary

I documented 22 failure modes for **kvstore**, organized as causal chains from root cause to user-visible symptom:

**Root causes (9)** — e.g. `fm-backing-file-os-io-failure`, `fm-storage-path-misconfigured-or-missing`, `fm-evictor-ttl-unit-mismatch-bug` (a real bug: TTL comparison mixes ms and s, so eviction never fires), `fm-admin-write-not-invalidating-cache`, `fm-storage-delimiter-not-escaped`, `fm-storage-put-non-atomic-read-modify-write`, `fm-storage-unbounded-linear-scan-design`, `fm-evictor-scheduling-unverifiable`, `fm-no-logging-anywhere`.

**Intermediate (2)** — `fm-storage-error-raised`, `fm-cache-entries-never-evicted`.

**User-visible ends (11)** — including a raised exception on read (`fm-get-value-request-fails`), unbounded memory growth, permanently stale reads after a write, a "negative cache poisoning" variant, silent `None` returns masking a misconfigured path, storage corruption from unescaped delimiters, lost updates and torn reads from missing locking, crash-truncation, and gradual latency decay.

Each entry carries a `coverage_status`:
- **alertable** (1): `fm-get-value-request-fails` — already covered by the existing `outcome=error` counter.
- **metric-gap** (19): real gaps needing new instrumentation before they're alertable — flagged for Phase 3.
- **excluded** (2, with reasoning): `fm-no-logging-anywhere` (cross-cutting deficiency, not a discrete alert target) and `fm-concurrent-read-during-write-torn-read` (impractical to detect independently; redundant with the lost-update alert).

Note: Phase 1 had already been finalized by the time I could submit it (frozen), and one entry id I chose (`fm-concurrent-write-lost-update`) collided with a pre-seeded one, which I updated in place rather than re-adding. Ready for review before Phase 3 (metric coverage).

Phase 3 -- metric coverage: inventory the metrics this codebase actually implements as
Metric entries (tied to where each is emitted in the code), then set every failure
mode's coverage status: `alertable` (implemented metrics suffice; only an alert rule is
missing), `metric-gap` (implemented metrics cannot detect it adequately; propose the
metric change needed), or `excluded` (record the reason). Every metric recommendation
must name the failure mode(s) it serves and state whether it is a new metric or a
change to an existing one. Propose every entry through `propose_edits`, tagged for
phase 3.

First principles for this analysis (spec, "What Blare is"):

- Alerting is the target. Documenting failure modes is the first step, not the goal;
  every failure mode must end in an alert recommendation or an explicit, reasoned
  exclusion.
- Failure chains, not just user-visible ends. A user-visible failure is usually the
  last link of a chain. Document the upstream links as failure modes in their own
  right so each can be detected as early as possible.

Inventory instrumentation already implemented in this codebase using any of:

- Python: the `prometheus_client` library (Counter, Gauge, Histogram, Summary
  definitions and their `.labels(...)` call sites).
- Go: `prometheus/client_golang` (`prometheus.NewCounter`/`NewGauge`/`NewHistogram`
  and their registration with a `prometheus.Registry`).
- Node.js: `prom-client` (`new Counter(...)`, `new Gauge(...)`, `new Histogram(...)`).
- Java/JVM: Micrometer's Prometheus registry (`PrometheusMeterRegistry`, meters
  registered against it).
- Any direct `/metrics` HTTP exposition endpoint, whichever library serves it.

A metric definition site is where a metric's name, type, and labels are declared —
not every place it is incremented or observed.

- `name`: the alert's identifier.
- `expr`: the PromQL expression that fires the alert, at most

- `for_duration`: how long the expression must hold before firing, as a Prometheus

payload_or_id.details: Increment in Storage.get/Storage.put wherever OSError is caught and wrapped as StorageError (kvstore/storage.py:29-30,44-45), labeled by operation (get/put).

payload_or_id.details: Increment in admin.update_value on every call, labeled outcome=success/error and invalidated_cache=true/false depending on whether cache.evict(key) was called (kvstore/admin.py:12-16).

payload_or_id.details: Increment (direction=write) in Storage.put when a key or value contains ',' or '\n' before serialization, and (direction=read) when a parsed line's reconstructed key/value doesn't round-trip cleanly (kvstore/storage.py:24-27,36-43).
payload_or_id.rationale: Storage's 'key,value' format is unescaped and currently fails silently -- no exception, no metric, just wrong data. This counter is the only proposed way to surface a collision/corruption event as it happens.

payload_or_id.details: Requires adding a monotonic version/mtime check to Storage.put (kvstore/storage.py:32-45): read the file's version before mutating, and increment this counter whenever the version has changed by the time the rewrite happens (a lost-update window was hit).
payload_or_id.rationale: There is no locking or compare-and-swap in Storage.put today, so concurrent writers silently clobber each other. This is a 'change' to Storage.put's own logic as well as a new metric, since detecting the conflict requires the version check to exist first.

payload_or_id.details: Requires Storage.put to write a trailing checksum/line-count marker and Storage.get to validate it on read (kvstore/storage.py:20-45), incrementing this counter when validation fails.
payload_or_id.rationale: write_text() is not atomic, so a crash mid-write leaves a truncated file that is currently parsed as silently-valid data with no error. Validation must be added before a failure of this kind can be observed at all.

payload_or_id.details: Set to the number of lines/entries in the backing file at the end of every Storage.put call (kvstore/storage.py:36-45).
payload_or_id.rationale: Storage never deletes and both get and put are O(total keys); a growing entry count is the leading indicator of the latency degradation this design causes, well before it shows up in request latency.

payload_or_id.details: Wrap the body of api.get_value (kvstore/api.py:26-33) with a Histogram.time()/observe() call.
payload_or_id.rationale: There is currently no latency instrumentation anywhere in the package; this is the direct, lagging confirmation to pair with the leading kvstore_storage_entry_count gauge for the same failure mode.
